# @comecaramelos/dsh-unity-mcp

> [!WARNING]
> **Deprecated.** This plugin is no longer maintained. Use
> dsh-mcp-manager instead: i

t
> connects the Unity relay (and any other MCP server) as a plain `stdio`
> connection. See Migrati
ng to dsh-mcp-manager.
## Migrating to dsh-mcp-manager
The manager requires dsh `^0.2.0`.
1. Remove this plugin:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If it still shows up in `dsh.profile.bundles` of the profile's
`package.json`, delete that line.
2. Install the manager:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

3. In **Plugins → MCP connections → MCP connections**, hit *Add connection* and
create a `stdio` con
nection with your old settings:
| dsh-unity-mcp | dsh-mcp-manager |

| `serverName` (`unity`) | `id` — keep `unity` so tools stay `mcp__unity__*` |
| **Unity relay execu

table** / `relayPath` | `command` |
| `--mcp` + **Extra flags** / `extraFlags` | `args`, one per lin

e, `--mcp` first |
| **Reduce log output** | stderr → *Log file* |
For example:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The rest of this README documents the plugin as it was.

Connects DSH to the **Unity MCP** server — the `unity-ai-relay` executable the
Unity AI Assistant pa

ckage (`com.unity.ai.assistant`) installs — through the
stock `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` stdio br

idge, plus a settings/status card in
the Web GUI.
Every tool the relay registers is exposed as a normal `mcp__unity__*` tool.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin **does not download anything**: it launches the `unity-ai-relay`
executable your Unity Ed

itor installed. Install the
Unity AI Assistant
package first, and keep a Unity Editor running — the

relay is the Editor's
side-channel, so an Editor that is not running answers
`No Unity Editor connec

is the Editor's
side-channel, so an Editor that is not running answers
`No Unity Editor connected`.
## Configuration
Settings live under **Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration → DSH Unity MCP**.

- **Unity relay executable** — the executable the bridge launches. Open the
picker, hit **Fetch exec

utables** to search this machine (the search also walks
every Windows user profile visible from a WS

L host), and pick one. The pick is
remembered; applying a different one restarts the connection.
- *

*Extra flags** — one flag per row, appended after the `--mcp` mode flag the
bridge always passes, fo

r example `--project-path=/home/roberto/game`,
`--name=MyProject`, `--log-level=debug`.
- **Reduce l

og output** — keeps the relay's own progress lines out of the DSH
console by redirecting its stderr

into a log file (turn it off to debug the
raw output).

Nothing is picked for you: what the saved rows list is what you can pick, and a
path you picked stay

s picked — if it later stops running it reads broken, it is
never silently re-resolved.
### Windows relay from WSL

A Windows relay launched through the WSL interop mount works like a native one:
it speaks MCP over s

tdio, so nothing about the connection changes. The card says
so when that is what is running, and re

minds you to keep the relay's arguments
(`--log-dir`, and `--project-path` when you pin a project) i

n their Windows
spelling — the relay resolves them on the Windows side.
## Row configuration
For a per-profile pin, edit the plugin row's `config`:
| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `serverName` | `unity` | the bridge's server namespace (tool names are `mcp__<serverName>__<tool>`

hs` | the platform's relay locations | the candidate list the **Search executables** run probes |
|

`extraFlags` | `[]` | flags appended after the `--mcp` mode flag |
| `command` | `""` | a launcher p

refix to wrap the spawn with (the relay needs no wrapper) |
| `env` / `cwd` | `{}` / `""` | passed t

hrough to the bridge |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `60000` | per-tool-call timeout |
| `failOnStartupErr

or` | `false` | fail the load when the bridge cannot start |
| `reconnect` | `{ enabled: true, initi

alDelayMs: 500, maxDelayMs: 30000, maxAttempts: 10 }` | reconnect policy |
| `bridgeStderr` | `"log"

` | console-output routing: `"log"` captures stderr into a log file, `"console"` echoes it |
| `brid
geStderrLog` | `""` | log path override for `"log"` mode (absolute paths only) |

The environment variable `DSH_UNITY_MCP_FLAGS` (whitespace-separated) seeds the
launch flags for one

nvironment variable `DSH_UNITY_MCP_FLAGS` (whitespace-separated) seeds the
launch flags for one run.
